standard_prerequisites.name: Very ample invertible sheaves and closed immersions into projective space
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the embedding making L a power of the restriction of O(1).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a closed-immersion pushforward and depth along finite ring maps

standard_prerequisites.use: Transfer cohomology and depth between F and the packaged sheaf G.

core_obligations: Choose a closed immersion i : X -> P^n_k with i^*O(1) isomorphic to L^{tensor e} for some e > 0 (proof lines 11169-11172).

Reduce to the sheaf G = i_*(F + F tensor L + ... + F tensor L^{tensor e-1}) on projective space, using that the cohomology of G(m) is the direct sum of the H^1(X, F tensor L^{tensor j+me}) (proof lines 11173-11187).
Verify the depth conditions for G: infinite depth off i(X) and depth equal to that of F_x at points i(x), using that the stalk is F_x^{oplus e} over the local ring (proof lines 11188-11195).
Carry out the projective-space case for X = P^n_k and L = O(1) with the depth hypothesis, which is the remaining body of the proof (proof lines 11197-11290).
proof_roadmap: Embed into projective space so that the ample sheaf becomes a power of O(1).
Package the twists into one coherent sheaf with the same depth behaviour.
Reduce the negative-twist vanishing to the projective-space case and prove it there.
difficulty_reason: The lemma, attributed by the author to Enriques-Severi-Zariski, proves that for a proper scheme X over a field, an ample invertible sheaf L and a coherent F whose stalks have depth at least two at all closed points, one has H^1(X, F tensor L^{tensor m}) = 0 for m sufficiently negative. The proof embeds X into projective space so that L becomes a power of the restriction of O(1), reduces to a coherent module G on projective space built from the e twists of F, checks that G again has depth at least two at closed points and infinite depth off the image, and then carries out the projective-space case (proof lines 11168-11290). H3: the reduction step that packages the e twists into a single sheaf with controlled depth, followed by the projective-space vanishing argument, is independent research-level work.
